newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Avis drives firm debut on S.Africa JSE.
newsitem.headline: Avis drives firm debut on S.Africa JSE.

text.p: Shares in South African tourism and car rental firm Avis Holdings Ltd made a strong debut on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Monday as they surged more than a third in value in early trade.
After opening at 625 cents, Avis shares motored higher to touch a best level of 700 cents in brisk trade. By 0835 GMT shares had edged back to 690 cents after 101,300 stocks had changed hands.
The listing forms part of the unbundling of Servgro International Ltd where Servgro shareholders received stocks in Avis at 470 cents a share. There was no public offer.
Dealers said stags -- investors who buy stocks in the hopes of selling them off quickly to make a profit -- were behind the early activity in Avis.
"Mainly its guys that are taking a punt on Servgro. They got the share at 4.70 and now they are making a two rand profit," one dealer said.

Dealers said Avis, which also has interests in fleet management, car sales, body shops and coach tours, would hold investors' interests due to the firm's good growth prospects coupled with a cheap share price.

Outside South Africa, the group has interests all over the Southern African region, owning Avis operations in Botswana, Namibia and Swaziland and managing Avis sub-licensees in Angola, Lesotho, Madagascar, Malawi, Mozambique, Zambia and Zimbabwe.
"I think the share will run around 6.80-7.00 rand for the rest of the day," another trader said.
In its pre-listing statement the firm forecast turnover of 393.2 million rand, earnings per share of 34.9 cents and a dividend of 8.03 cents a share.
